transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12T15:00:00-07:00
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Emma Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Lena Chen (Aurora CISO), Mark Rivers (Aurora Head of Platform), Darla Singh (Aurora Security Engineer)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Aurora's security posture and whether Redwood's hosted or dedicated/private options meet their controls (SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/encryption, data retention). Agreed next steps include sharing SOC2 docs and scheduling technical deep-dive for dedicated deployment and KMS integration.

Topics:
- Compliance posture (SOC2 / ISO)
- Authentication & IAM (SSO/SAML, RBAC)
- Auditability (logs, retention, access trails)
- Encryption and KMS options (customer-managed keys)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
- Pilot and benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro on our side, I'm Emma, AE at Redwood Inference, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Diego: Hi all, thanks for making time.
[00:10] Lena: Hi, Lena here, CISO at Aurora. Mark and Darla are with me.
[00:14] Mark: Hey.
[00:16] Darla: Hi.
[00:18] Emma: Great. High level we understand you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated/private and security is front and center. Would love to hear your current stack and main controls needed.
[00:27] Lena: Sure. We're a mid-size fintech, a lot of regs. We need SOC 2 Type II, working on ISO 27001, strong SSO, SAML-based integration, RBAC with least-privilege, full audit logs, and customer-managed keys ideally. Also retention policies — some data must be retained for seven years, others shorter.
[00:45] Emma: Totally. We support SOC2 and we publish our attestation; for ISO we have a roadmap, happy to share interim docs. On SSO we support SAML and OIDC and you can map groups to roles for RBAC.
[00:57] Lena: How does RBAC map to model access? We want to limit who can call production models and who can spin up dedicated capacity.
[01:06] Diego: Right — so Redwood's RBAC is role- and route-based. We have admin, operator, observer roles out of the box; you can create custom roles and scope them to projects and endpoints. For dedicated environments we can integrate with your IdP so provisioning is automated.
[01:20] Darla: When you say integrate with our IdP, are there options for SCIM provisioning or just SAML assertions?
[01:26] Diego: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning — sometimes folks use SAML only for auth and SCIM for user sync. There may be some naming noise depending on IdP but most work out of the box with Azure AD and Okta.
[01:37] Mark: On the encryption front, can you explain KMS options? We need to know if we can bring our own keys (BYOK).
[01:44] Emma: Yes, frequent ask. For Redwood Hosted we offer platform-managed keys by default but there is a customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated and Private deployments. Diego, want to add the technical nuance?
[01:55] Diego: Sure. In Dedicated we can connect to your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSM) for disk and egress key wrapping. For hosted we can enable envelope encryption with a CMK in some cases — but full BYOK where the key never leaves your control is typically on private deployments or dedicated VPCs with dedicated key access.
[02:14] Lena: Is there an attestation that keys never leave provider boundary? This is important for our auditors.
[02:20] Diego: For private on-prem or VPC deployments we can run a model where the key material is in your KMS and Redwood components call KMS APIs in your project. We have documentation and a security runbook showing key flow; we'll share the diagrams.
[02:34] Lena: Okay, good.
[02:36] Emma: Audit logs — we log admin actions, model deployments, API calls with token-level metadata, and can ship logs to your SIEM over syslog or cloud logging. Darla, is that aligned with what you need?
[02:47] Darla: Mostly. We need immutable audit trails, retention policy enforcement, and proof of tamper resistance for some logs. Can you forward logs to our Splunk instance?
[02:56] Diego: Yes, we can forward to Splunk, Datadog, or push to cloud storage. For immutability, we support write-once policies if you configure your storage that way on your side; Redwood preserves the log integrity but the storage guarantees come from the target.
[03:11] Darla: Makes sense. Do you support log signing or checksum verification?
[03:15] Diego: Not currently as built-in log-signing, most customers do checksums and use cloud storage object versioning + access controls. We can discuss a hardened pipeline in the SE deep-dive.
[03:25] Mark: Data residency — we have EU and US customers; can we pin data to regions?
[03:30] Emma: Yes, Redwood Hosted supports region controls; you can route requests to region-specific clusters. For strong guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where the compute and storage are fully within the region or VPC.
[03:42] Lena: What about data retention and deletion? We need the ability to delete logs and data on demand and to enforce retention windows.
[03:49] Diego: We have retention policies per project that you can configure; for Hosted there's a managed retention layer and we can process deletion requests. For Dedicated/Private you control retention in your environment. Important note: model caching (prefix/KV cache) can keep transient tokens — we document cache retention and provide hooks to clear caches on-demand.
[04:10] Lena: You mentioned KV cache — can you say that again?
[04:13] Diego: Yeah, it's our runtime cache for recent context. Sometimes transcription and docs call it "K-V" or "K caching"; sorry if earlier calls had different terms. It's important for repeat prompt performance but if you have retention constraints we can disable or shorten it.
[04:26] Emma: Another common auditor ask is separation of duties and privileged access reviews. We support audit reports and can provide a list of people with infra access.
[04:35] Lena: Are Redwood engineers ever able to access customer data in Hosted?
[04:40] Emma: By default no; we have access controls. For debugging we have a secure support workflow — customers can opt-in to share traces or request a sanitized debug collection. All access is audited and requires approval.
[04:51] Darla: Ok good. About SOC2 — do you have an up-to-date Type II report we can review?
[04:55] Emma: Yes, I'll send the SOC 2 Type II attestation and our security pack after the call.
[04:59] Lena: For our procurement, we also need contractual terms around data processing and breach notification windows.
[05:05] Emma: We have standard DPA language and breach SLA options for enterprise customers. Diego will capture the necessary certs for the contract team.
[05:12] Diego: Will do.
[05:14] Mark: On the performance side, we're evaluating latency — sometimes teams pick hosted for ease but worry about PII or latencies. Is there a common pattern you recommend?
[05:24] Emma: Many fintechs start with Hosted in a restricted region with strict network controls and then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and BYOK/KMS needs.
[05:33] Diego: For latency-critical endpoints we recommend dedicated capacity pinned to specific hardware; that gives you consistent p99s. We can run a benchmark with your sample traffic in our pilot.
[05:43] Mark: That would help.
[05:45] Darla: A couple more detail questions: 1) Are API keys logged in plaintext in logs? 2) Can we centralize secrets in our vault and not in Redwood?
[05:54] Diego: 1) No, secrets like API keys are redacted in logs; we record token metadata but not the secret itself. 2) We support integrating with external secret stores for dedicated/private. For Hosted we have encrypted secret storage and can integrate via HashiCorp Vault in enterprise setups.
[06:08] Lena: For SSO, we need SCIM provisioning with automated group mappings. Can Redwood map SCIM groups to model permissions?
[06:17] Emma: Yes, group mapping is supported, and Diego can show the role mapping matrix in the follow-up.
[06:23] Diego: We'll surface the mapping matrix and sample policy snippets.
[06:27] [short pause as someone shares a doc link]
[06:30] Mark: One area of concern — can you talk about vulnerability management, patching schedule for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:36] Diego: Hosted is patched by our infra team with a documented schedule and emergency patching for CVEs. For Dedicated and Private, we offer a managed ops option where Redwood applies patches during maintenance windows; for fully on-prem customers they control patching but we provide the recommended schedule and patches.
[06:52] Darla: And for image provenance — do you sign your runtime images?
[06:56] Diego: We use signed artifacts and can provide SBOMs and image signatures on request.
[07:02] Lena: Good. For the auditors, we need a network diagram showing flow between Aurora VPC, Redwood control plane, and any third-party services.
[07:10] Emma: We'll include that in the package. We'll also include an architecture diagram showing KMS flows.
[07:16] Lena: Excellent. Are there any blockers for us to run a pilot? What information do you need?
[07:22] Diego: We'll need sample payloads (sanitized), expected QPS and p99 latency targets, list of IP ranges to allow if you want IP allowlisting, and whether you want BYOK or cloud-managed keys.
[07:32] Mark: We can provide those. On IP allowlist, do you support private peering or direct connect?
[07:38] Emma: For Dedicated we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and direct connect options depending on cloud. For Hosted we support IP allowlisting and link-based VPNs in some regions.
[07:49] Darla: Is there an SLA for data deletion requests?
[07:53] Diego: We have documented deletion workflows; for enterprise customers we can agree to a contractual window — typically 30 days for removal from active stores and longer for backup windows unless otherwise agreed. We'll provide specifics in the DPA draft.
[08:06] Lena: About backups — are backups encrypted with the same KMS?
[08:10] Diego: Yes, backups use the same KMS keys in a dedicated deployment; for Hosted they're encrypted with platform keys unless you enable CMK options where supported.
[08:19] Emma: Quick note — some customers used Anthropic/OpenAI earlier and ask about output consistency. Not directly security but helps set expectations.
[08:26] Lena: We're aware of those vendors. Our main focus is controls and data residency.
[08:30] Emma: Understood.
[08:32] [15 min marker—lightly jump ahead to negotiation topics]
[23:30] Mark: If we proceed with Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline?
[23:34] Diego: Typically 6-8 weeks for Dedicated with standard configs; if you need on-prem or air-gapped it can be 10-14 weeks depending on approvals.
[23:43] Lena: And cost — we'll want pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated and the incremental cost for KMS/BYOK and extra retention.
[23:49] Emma: We'll send a pricing sheet with committed capacity options and add-on pricing for managed KMS, extended log retention, and premium SLA.
[23:59] Darla: Make sure the pricing includes a support SLA — we need incident response times.
[24:04] Emma: Noted.
[24:06] Diego: One technical detail — when you bring your own KMS in Dedicated, we recommend rotating keys per your policy; we support automated rotation with zero-downtime key swapping. We'll include a runbook.
[24:18] Lena: Okay. On the compliance docs, we need proof of penetration testing and third-party attestation.
[24:24] Emma: We have pen test summaries and vulnerability assessment reports; I'll bundle appropriate redacted reports in the package.
[24:31] Lena: For legal, we need DPA, SOC2, and ISO roadmap.
[24:35] Emma: We'll include DPA and SOC2. The ISO materials are in progress—I'll flag that in the note.
[24:42] [wrap-up]
[24:45] Emma: To recap: Emma will share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and security pack by Friday. Diego will prepare pilot runbook and role mapping matrix and propose times for a dedicated SE deep-dive. Aurora will share sanitized sample payloads, desired latency targets, IP allowlist needs, and data retention policy.
[25:04] Lena: Yep — we'll get those over.
[25:07] Mark: Sounds good.
[25:09] Darla: Thanks.
[25:11] Emma: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with artifacts and propose times.
[25:15] [call ends — approximate duration 42 minutes]

Notes on transcription quality: Some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed variably). There are short overlaps and filler words.
